Spec review companion · #156 · snapshot eb02af5 · 2026-11-09

Copy the logged-in accounts into the plugin's Copilot folder

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug triage · #156

The change

With the token in the Linux keyring, setup, reviews and read-only tasks say "not logged in". Copilot finds the login on its own, but not with the plugin's own Copilot folder. assessment.md:50

Fix: before each read-only start, the plugin copies the host and login of each logged-in account, never a token, from the user's config.json into its own one. fix.md:10

8file groups changed fix.md:19
7tests added or updated fix.md:46
6checks passed test.md:20
1check not run (Linux) test.md:19
1deviation in force (a docs sentence); one more was taken out again fix.md:61

Root cause

Copilot CLI 1.0.105 on that Linux system finds a keyring login only through the account names in its own config.json. The plugin's folder has none. assessment.md:82

Remediation

Copy the names field by field, keep the plugin file's other keys and comment lines, remove the names after a logout, write only on a change. assessment.md:91

Copilot's config.json starts with two // comment lines, so plain JSON.parse fails on every real file. Neither blind plan saw this. assessment.md:34

How it works

Examples

These are the tests and checks that ran. The Linux keyring case did not run.

Token-like fields

A user entry with token, a token map and extra fields gives only host and login in the plugin file. This is the security promise. fix.md:46

Logout and switch

No keys, a missing file, a folder in its place, broken JSON, a wrong shape: each removes the names. A switch shows the new account. fix.md:47

No rewrite

The same accounts in Copilot's own formatting cause no write. This keeps the race with Copilot's own writes small. fix.md:48

Write failure

A folder in place of the plugin file stops the run before Copilot starts; setup shows the error, not "not logged in". fix.md:50

Real Windows setup

Setup from the branch with a new data folder reports "logged in" and copies nothing. test.md:20

What to check before approving

  1. The Linux reproduction did not run. The fix rests on the reporter's probe that the two keys alone make Copilot find the keyring login. test.md:19 test.md:40
  2. The keys are not in the Copilot docs. A later version can move them; the copy then copies nothing, which is today's behaviour. assessment.md:198 test.md:42
  3. Lost write accepted. A Copilot process from an earlier job can write the plugin file between the read and the rename. assessment.md:174
  4. The setup step still shows with every "not logged in". The plugin cannot see where Copilot kept the token, so it names the case instead. assessment.md:118

On purpose, the plugin does not look for a token key in the user's file. assessment.md:128

# Bug Assessment: setup says "not logged in" when the token is in the Linux keyring - **Slug**: 156-copy-logged-in-accounts- **Created**: 2026-11-09- **Source**: pasted text (issue #156, with facts checked on 2026-11-09 on Windows 11 with Copilot CLI 1.0.105)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: high ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Issue #156. On Ubuntu 26.10 (GNOME Keyring serving `org.freedesktop.secrets`), Copilot CLI 1.0.105,plugin 1.0.25: after `copilot login --device-code` prints `Signed in successfully as tmathura.`, and`copilot -p "Reply with the single word OK."` answers, `/copilot:setup` still reports`ready: false` and `auth.detail: "not logged in"`. Every review and read-only task fails the sameway. The next steps include "On a system without a credential store, `copilot login` saves thetoken in a file that the plugin cannot read. Set `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` …", which does not apply:the system has a credential store and the token is in it. The reporter's probe, outside the plugin: - `COPILOT_HOME=<empty folder> copilot -p "Reply with the single word OK."` gives  `Error: No authentication information found.`- With a `COPILOT_HOME` whose `config.json` holds only `lastLoggedInUser` and `loggedInUsers`  (each entry `{host, login}`, no token), the same command prints `OK`. Workaround: merge those two keys (only `host` and `login`) from `~/.copilot/config.json` into theplugin's `copilot-home/config.json`. Setup then reports ready. On Windows 11 with Copilot CLI 1.0.101 (2026-11-02), neither file has these keys and setup reports"logged in". Facts checked for this assessment (2026-11-09, Windows 11, Copilot CLI 1.0.105): - Copilot's `config.json` is not plain JSON. `~/.copilot/config.json` and the plugin's  `copilot-home/config.json` both start with two comment lines,  `// User settings belong in settings.json.` and `// This file is managed automatically.`, then a  JSON object. `JSON.parse` on the raw text fails.- Here `~/.copilot/config.json` has the keys `firstLaunchAt`, `appTipShown`,  `reasoningSummariesCleanupDone` and `askedSetupTerminals`, and no account keys. The plugin's file  has only `firstLaunchAt`. Setup reports "logged in".- The Copilot CLI docs ("Authenticating GitHub Copilot CLI", "Troubleshooting Copilot CLI  authentication") say that when the system keychain is unavailable, "the CLI prompts you to store  the token in a plaintext configuration file at `~/.copilot/config.json`", with the prompt  "System keychain unavailable. Store token in plaintext config file? (y/N)". They name no key for  that token, and they do not mention `lastLoggedInUser` or `loggedInUsers`. The CLI binary is  packed, so its key names cannot be read from it. ## Symptom With the token in the OS keyring, Copilot run with the plugin's own `COPILOT_HOME` does not findthe login, so setup, reviews and read-only tasks fail with "not logged in". They should find thesame login that `copilot` finds when it runs on its own. ## Reproduction 1. On Linux with a running Secret Service (GNOME Keyring) and Copilot CLI 1.0.105, run   `copilot login --device-code` and approve it.2. Run `copilot -p "Reply with the single word OK."`. It prints `OK`.3. Run `node plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs setup --json`. It reports   `ready: false`, `auth.detail: "not logged in"`. Not reproduced in this session: it needs that Linux system. The Windows system here shows theother side: no account keys in either file, and setup reports "logged in". ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:172` `buildCopilotEnv()` — for a read-only run it  replaces the caller's `COPILOT_HOME` with the plugin's folder (`resolveCopilotHome`, line 168).- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:428` `runCopilotTurn()` — creates that folder (line  440) and puts nothing in it. Reviews, the review gate, read-only tasks and the login check all start Copilot  here.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:581` `getCopilotAuthStatus()` — the login check runs  through `runCopilotTurn`, and reads `No authentication information found` as "not logged in"  (`NOT_LOGGED_IN_PATTERN`, line 64).- `plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs:227` `buildSetupReport()` — adds the "system  without a credential store" step to every "not logged in" result, stated as the cause.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs:444` `writeJsonAtomic()` — the temp file and rename writer  with mode 0600 that the state files use. It is private to that module. ## Root Cause Hypothesis On this Linux setup, Copilot CLI 1.0.105 finds a keyring login only through the account names thatit records in `config.json` under its home (`lastLoggedInUser`, `loggedInUsers`). The plugin'sread-only home has no such names, so Copilot never asks the keyring and reports no login. Thetoken never was in `config.json`, so the plugin's folder needs only the names. Confidence: high forthe mechanism (the reporter's probe shows the two keys alone turn the failure into `OK`); mediumfor which platforms or versions write these keys (Windows with 1.0.101 and 1.0.105 writes none). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: before each read-only Copilot start in `runCopilotTurn` (so also before the logincheck), copy the account names from the user's Copilot folder into the plugin's one: - Read `config.json` in the caller's `COPILOT_HOME` (from `options.env ?? process.env`, because  the environment that `buildCopilotEnv` builds has the plugin's folder there), or in `~/.copilot`  when it is not set. Drop whole-line `//` comments before `JSON.parse`, because Copilot writes  two of them at the top. Only whole lines count, so a value such as `"https://..."` is kept.- Keep only well-formed entries, and from each only `host` and `login` (both strings):  `lastLoggedInUser` (one entry) and `loggedInUsers` (a list; an empty result is left out). An  entry of another shape, a `loggedInUsers` that is not a list, or a root that is not an object  gives nothing and does not throw. Never copy any other field, so no token can be copied.- Read the plugin's `config.json` the same way (a missing or broken file counts as empty, so a  broken file loses its other keys when accounts are copied; Copilot writes only `firstLaunchAt`  there). Remove the two keys from it, add the copied ones, and keep every other key and the  comment lines at its top. A new file gets no comment lines; Copilot adds its own.- When the user's file is missing, cannot be read (for example a folder in its place), is broken,  or has no such keys, the two keys are removed from the plugin's file, so a logout or an account  switch is picked up on the next run.- Write only when the two account keys change (compared as parsed values, not as text, because  Copilot may format the file in its own way), through a temp file and a rename, with mode 0600. The state  module's JSON writer is split into an atomic text writer, which this copy uses, and the JSON  writer on top of it, so the state files keep their format. When there is nothing to copy and  the plugin's file does not exist, write nothing, so Windows and macOS stay as today.- A failed write of the plugin's file fails the run before Copilot starts, with the error: Copilot  could not use that folder either. The login check then reports that error, not "not logged in".- Write runs are not changed: they use the user's own folder. For the next step, the docs name no key for a file-stored token, so the plugin cannot tell thatcase without guessing a key. Word the step as a condition the user can check: "If `copilot login`asked to store the token in a plaintext config file (no system keychain), the plugin cannot readit. …", still naming `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. `plugins/copilot/commands/setup.md` (its output rule)and the README item on setup's next steps say the same. Doc passages that become false and change: `docs/configuration.md` "Log in" (the credential storeline) and "Systems without a credential store", the "Permission profiles" notes on the plugin'sfolder, and `docs/operations.md` "Clean up" ("It holds no login"). **Alternatives**: - Copy the whole user `config.json` into the plugin's folder: simpler, but it can carry a  plaintext token and the user's other settings into the plugin's folder. Rejected.- Run read-only Copilot with the user's own `COPILOT_HOME`: finds every login, but brings back the  user's trusted folders, hooks, saved approvals and MCP servers, which the plugin's folder keeps  out (constitution Principle IV). Rejected.- Look for a token key in the user's file to decide on the next step: the key is not documented,  and reading it is close to reading a token. Rejected. **Files likely to change**: - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs`- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` (an exported atomic text writer under the JSON writer)- `plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs` (the next step's words)- `plugins/copilot/commands/setup.md` (the output rule for that step)- `tests/copilot.test.mjs`, `tests/runtime-setup.test.mjs`- `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/operations.md`, `README.md`- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (patch release 1.0.26) **Tests to add or update**: - A user `config.json` with the comment lines, `lastLoggedInUser` and `loggedInUsers` entries  with extra fields and a token-like field gives a plugin `config.json` with only `host` and  `login`, no token text, its own comment lines and `firstLaunchAt` kept, and mode 0600 on  non-Windows.- A user file with no such keys, a missing user file and a broken user file each remove the keys  from the plugin's file and keep its other keys; so do a root that is not an object and a  `loggedInUsers` that is not a list. Mixed entries keep only the well-formed ones. A value with  `//` inside it does not break the parse.- A user `config.json` that cannot be read (a folder in its place) copies nothing.- A new plugin file (keys to copy, no file yet) holds only the copied keys. A broken plugin file,  or one whose root is not an object, is replaced by one with only the copied keys.- A second run with the same accounts does not rewrite the plugin's file, also when its  formatting differs from the plugin's.- A plugin `config.json` that cannot be written (a folder in its place) fails the read-only run  before Copilot starts and leaves no temp file in `copilot-home`; the login check reports the  error, not "not logged in", so setup gives no login steps.- The caller's `COPILOT_HOME` is read; without it, `~/.copilot` is read (a setup run with `HOME`  and `USERPROFILE` set to a temp folder, which also covers the login check).- A write run does not touch the plugin's file.- With nothing to copy and no plugin file, no plugin file is written.- The setup next step is worded as a condition. ## Risks & Considerations - Copilot rewrites its own `config.json`. A Copilot run that starts after the copy reads the copied  names. Two plugin runs that start at the same time write the same text, and the rename keeps the  file whole. A Copilot process that is still running from an earlier job can write the plugin's  file between the plugin's read and its rename; that write is then lost. The window is one read  and one rename, and the write happens only when the accounts change, so this risk is accepted.- On Windows a rename can fail for a moment while another process has the file open; the state  writer already retries that. Writing only on a change keeps this rare.- Copilot may change the format or the keys in a later version. A missing or changed key then  copies nothing, which is today's behaviour.- The copied names (`host`, `login`) are not secret, but the file is still made owner-only.- A `/copilot:setup` on Linux cannot be checked in CI against the real keyring; tests use the fake  CLI. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. The change stays inside the adapter (`copilot.mjs`), the state  module and setup's next steps; no file, command or function is renamed. The difference from  upstream (Codex has no per-plugin Copilot folder) is added to the existing `COPILOT_HOME` item  in the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin", with its reason (platform support).- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. All code is written in this repo, with Node built-ins only.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met, with a note. Only the adapter  starts Copilot and decides its environment. The two keys are not in the Copilot docs; the plugin  only copies them when they are there, and copies nothing when they are not, so an undocumented  change cannot widen permissions. `setup` still reports a missing login clearly.- **IV. Safe by default**: met. Read-only runs keep the plugin's own folder with none of the user's  trusted folders, hooks, approvals or MCP servers. No token is copied: only `host` and `login`  strings are taken, field by field. The file is written with mode 0600. No shell runs.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. Paths go through `node:path` and `os.homedir()`; the writer retries  the Windows rename; CI runs on ubuntu, macOS and Windows. Windows and macOS with no such keys  write nothing.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. The fake CLI tests cover a missing, broken and  key-less user file, the token filter, the kept keys, the write run, and the login check. The  release run covers setup on Windows.

# Bug Fix: setup says "not logged in" when the token is in the Linux keyring - **Slug**: 156-copy-logged-in-accounts- **Fixed**: 2026-11-09- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary Before each read-only Copilot start, also the login check, the plugin now copies the `host` and`login` of the logged-in accounts from the user's Copilot `config.json` into its own one, andremoves them there when the user's file has none. Setup's plaintext-token step is worded as acondition the user can check. Patch release 1.0.26. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs` | modified | `readCopilotConfig`, `pickAccount`, `pickLoggedInAccounts`, `copyLoggedInAccounts`; `runCopilotTurn` calls the copy in its read-only branch; file notice updated || `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` | modified | `writeFileAtomic` (exported text writer); `writeJsonAtomic` now calls it || `plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs` | modified | the `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` next step is worded as a condition || `plugins/copilot/commands/setup.md` | modified | the output rule for that step || `tests/copilot.test.mjs` | added tests | `setUp` gives each test an empty user Copilot folder || `tests/runtime-setup.test.mjs` | added test, updated test | the `~/.copilot` default; the step's wording || `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/operations.md`, `README.md` | modified | what the plugin's folder holds, and the step || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files | modified | 1.0.26 | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jsconst { lastLoggedInUser, loggedInUsers, ...rest } = current?.config ?? {};const copied = Object.fromEntries(  Object.entries({ lastLoggedInUser, loggedInUsers }).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined));if (isDeepStrictEqual(copied, accounts)) {  return;}``` The write happens only when the two keys differ from what the user's file gives, compared asvalues. A missing plugin file with nothing to copy, and a broken plugin file with nothing tocopy, both compare equal (`{}`), so nothing is written. ## Tests Added or Updated - `tests/copilot.test.mjs` "a read-only run copies only the host and login of the logged-in accounts into the plugin's Copilot folder" — the comment lines, a token-like field, a token map, extra fields, bad entries and a `//` inside a value; the plugin file keeps its comment lines and `firstLaunchAt`, drops stale accounts, has no token text, no temp file, and mode 0600 on macOS and Linux.- `tests/copilot.test.mjs` "the plugin's Copilot folder follows an account switch, and loses the accounts when the user's config has none" — a switch over two runs; no keys, a missing file, a folder in its place, a broken file, a root that is not an object, and a `loggedInUsers` that is not a list.- `tests/copilot.test.mjs` "the plugin's Copilot config is written only when its accounts change" — nothing written with nothing to copy; a new file holds only the accounts; the same accounts in Copilot's own formatting cause no rewrite; a broken plugin file is replaced.- `tests/copilot.test.mjs` "a write run does not touch the plugin's Copilot config".- `tests/copilot.test.mjs` "a plugin Copilot config that cannot be written stops a read-only run before Copilot starts" — no Copilot run, no temp file left, and the login check reports the error with no login steps.- `tests/runtime-setup.test.mjs` "the login check copies the accounts from ~/.copilot when COPILOT_HOME is not set" — a setup run with `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` set to a temp folder.- `tests/runtime-setup.test.mjs` "setup without a login names copilot login and the token variable" — the step is worded as a condition. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm run build` → passed; `node --test tests/copilot.test.mjs tests/runtime-setup.test.mjs` → 44 passed, 2 skipped (POSIX-only, on Windows). After review round 2: `npm test` → 524 tests, 482 passed, 0 failed, 42 skipped.- Manual checks: none. The Linux keyring case needs the reporter's system. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-11-09, review round 1: on Windows, the caller's `COPILOT_HOME` was found under any letter  case of its name, with a Windows-only test. Rejected in review round 2 and taken out: every  real caller passes the companion's own `process.env` (the review gate starts the companion as a  child process), and on Windows `process.env` already ignores letter case. So the lookup reads  `env.COPILOT_HOME`, as the assessment says.- 2026-11-09, review round 1: `docs/configuration.md` now says the plugin writes its  `config.json` readable only by you, not that the file always is: Copilot may write it with its  own mode. ## Follow-ups - The owner can check on the Linux system of the report that setup reports ready after the update.
